classification.difficultyReason: Find quadratic intersections, sketch each pair, identify the upper curve and integrate its difference using the explicitly taught procedure.

content.prompt: Solve simultaneously, sketch, shade the enclosed region, and find its area for:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x+3&=x^2+1\\x^2-x-2&=0\\(x-2)(x+1)&=0\\x&=2\text{ or }x=-1.\end{aligned}$$
The intersections are $(2,5)$ and $(-1,2)$. The line is above the parabola on $[-1,2]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-1}^{2}\big((x+3)-(x^2+1)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_{-1}^{2}(x-x^2+2)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}+2x\right]_{-1}^{2}\\&=\left(2-\frac83+4\right)-\left(\frac12+\frac13-2\right)\\&=\frac92\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Unticked axes, rising line and upward parabola with vertex above the origin. Complete solution adds the requested enclosed-region shading.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}9-x^2&=3-x\\x^2-x-6&=0\\(x-3)(x+2)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }x=-2.\end{aligned}$$
The intersections are $(3,0)$ and $(-2,5)$. The parabola is above the line on $[-2,3]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-2}^{3}\big((9-x^2)-(3-x)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_{-2}^{3}(6+x-x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[6x+\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{3}\\&=\left(18+\frac92-9\right)-\left(-12+2+\frac83\right)\\&=\frac{125}{6}\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$
